source.description: A worldwide research snapshot spanning films, serials, television movies, series, soap operas and individual episodes across forty-seven themes. The expanded index now includes women who knowingly or unknowingly bargain with a devil- or demon-coded force to become pregnant or have a child, with the pregnancy outcome stated; women hypnotized or mind-controlled by a husband, boyfriend, ex-husband or ex-boyfriend, with direct matches separated from third-party, occult, adult-audience and unresolved variants; adult-audience films and television in which hypnosis, possession or mind control overlaps a pregnancy or causes it; the worldwide adult-audience search for mothers controlled by a current husband or boyfriend; wives who are already mothers becoming pregnant by another man; partnered women hypnotized or mind-controlled into infidelity; the 174-entry worldwide adult-audience sweep of wives and other adult female characters subjected to hypnosis, mesmerism, hypnotic suggestion, erotic supernatural thrall or explicitly framed occult trance; wives and other female characters forcibly hypnotized into obedience; stepmothers or bonus moms hypnotized, possessed, cursed or enchanted against their will; pregnant stepmothers and bonus moms; the closest documented cases of a remarried wife controlled by her new husband or a stepfather figure; a pregnant single mother controlled by her new husband or child’s stepfather; pregnant women controlled by unborn, ghost or alien children; female characters controlled by children or teens; current wives controlled or possessed by a husband’s former wife or lover; wives hypnotized or controlled by therapists; parents being intimate while children sleep; the expanded worldwide index of children interrupting or witnessing their parents’ intimate moments; adoption followed by pregnancy; human-villain hypnosis; vampire mesmerism; demonic and occult control; spirit or djinn possession; tantrik and vashikaran plots; sci-fi control; cult brainwashing; therapeutic hypnosis; fantasy enchantment; and the expanded worldwide index of pregnant characters in sexual, sensual, romantic, attempted, labor-related or fantasy scenes.

source.research_notes_html:
Boundaries & open questions

Woman bargains with the devil or a demon for pregnancy / a child: 9 core matches + 1 failed-deal variant + 11 unresolved leads

The 30 September 2026 multilingual sweeps now support nine core records: six knowing feature-film cases, one knowing short and two unknowing fertility schemes. A high-confidence episode in which both fertility rituals fail is separated as a variant, and eleven thinner or structurally adjacent leads are not counted as verified core matches. Every card states the pregnancy outcome and the evidence caveat.

  • New verified additions: Pengabdi Setan / Satan's Slaves and Soulful are high confidence; Exorcismo Negro is medium-high confidence with a witch-mediated devil link; and the erotic-horror film Secta Sinestra / Bloody Sect is a medium-confidence tricked fertility-clinic case.
  • Failed-deal variant: American Horror Story: Coven “Boy Parts” is high confidence on plot, but Cordelia's paid and sex-magic fertility rituals do not result in pregnancy. The counterparty is practitioner Marie Laveau rather than the devil directly.
  • Source discrepancies retained: The Surrogate now says “pregnancy outcome ambiguous” because its pre-production pitch says she cannot get pregnant while release loglines say she struggles to stay pregnant. The American Horror Stories “BA'AL” card now records that Liv's husband faked the haunting; only the final beat suggests the real Ba'al may take hold.
  • Adult / R-rated / erotic search: one medium-confidence tricked case—Secta Sinestra—survived the worldwide search, but no title verified a knowing bargain. This is a documented search result, not proof that no other title exists.
  • Structural pattern: the knowing-deal protagonists are childless or barren, except the already-pregnant woman in Soulful, whose bargain seeks a healthy birth. No verified title was found in which an existing mother bargains for another child.
  • Common exclusions: the deal seeks wealth, beauty, revenge or saving a life; the child is the price rather than the object; a husband or family member makes the deal; or the woman is impregnated, possessed or cursed without making any bargain. Rosemary's Baby, Devil's Due, The First Omen, Pari, Impetigore and AHS: Delicate therefore remain outside this exact category.
  • Regional result: verified core cases remain concentrated in Indonesian / Malay-language horror, with Nigerian, Brazilian, Spanish and U.S. examples. No verified soap-opera or telenovela title surfaced, and thin regional-horror indexing remains an open documentation gap.
Pregnant sexual pleasure scenes: 5 verified additions from a worldwide sweep

The 30 September 2026 multilingual sweep added five deduplicated titles to the existing pregnancy-sex section: two high-confidence, one medium-high-confidence and two medium-confidence findings. Each card states whether pleasure is directly verified, inferred from pregnancy-era intimacy, or supported through scene dialogue and reviews.

  • Marital comedy: Catastrophe S2E1 shows deeply pregnant Sharon and Rob mid-coitus when their son walks in; it also appears in the child-walk-in category.
  • Erotic drama and arthouse intimacy: A Frozen Flower establishes the Queen’s new pregnancy before a passionate library encounter; Los días que vendrán contains explicit couple sexuality during pregnancy, though no source specifically documents moaning.
  • R-rated comedy and affair / new partner: How to Plan an Orgy in a Small Town depicts a heavily pregnant participant reaching orgasm; the Nollywood film The Pregnant Widow has a consensual steamy scene with a new partner, but its exact release year remains unverified.
  • Search boundary: 18 borderlines or unresolved leads and 81 unique near-misses were reviewed. More than 20 regional or format veins returned no verified match, including the worldwide adult / erotic plot-index pass at high confidence. This is a documentation result, not proof that no other title exists.
  • Not promoted: Titane, Jamón, jamón and Rosemary Is Pregnant Again remain outside the catalog because the pregnancy timing, pleasure element or direct participation could not be established strongly enough.
Partner hires a third party to hypnotize or mind-control wife / girlfriend: 4 verified

This worldwide multilingual sweep found four verified matches: three research additions and one upgraded existing catalog record. It is the rarest node in this trope family: stories more often make the partner the controller, use an uncommissioned villain, or rely on a communal conspiracy.

  • Verified motives: regain her love or stop her leaving (Maalaala Mo Kaya “Gayuma”); change or “cure” her behavior (While You Were Sleeping); extract a secret about a suspected rival (Tee Ratra); and malicious elimination for inheritance and another relationship (Sleep, My Love).
  • Honest-zero regions: Latin America and Spain, including telenovelas; the Middle East and Turkey; Europe; Japan; Chinese-language markets; Thailand; Indonesia; sub-Saharan Africa; and adult / erotic indexes worldwide.
  • Evidence boundary: the partner must arrange a third party and the wife, girlfriend or fiancée must herself be subjected to hypnosis, mind control, brainwashing or magical will override. Ordinary manipulation, self-performed control and the wrong target are excluded.
Female controlled by husband, boyfriend or ex-partner: direct matches, variants and honest zeroes

The 30 September 2026 worldwide multilingual sweep creates one unified partner-controller view while preserving the existing plot categories on every record. It found three newly verified relationship readings: current boyfriend Victor repeatedly hypnotizes Ciça in O Beijo do Vampiro; a psychopathic “lover” hypnotizes the woman in Silence of Sleep; and ex-boyfriend Rodrigo repeatedly hypnotizes Amália in Caminhos do Coração. Scott Pilgrim vs. the World was already cataloged and now gains explicit ex-boyfriend membership.

  • Current husband: seven direct hypnosis cases and two broader-control cases are grouped separately from one disputed synopsis and partner-instigated third-party variants. The husband re-pass found no net-new title beyond records already in the catalog.
  • Current boyfriend: O Beijo do Vampiro is high confidence; Silence of Sleep is medium confidence because the source says “lover,” not formal boyfriend. Petite Mort has been corrected to an excluded prior lead: it is a German / Austrian torture-house horror with no verified hypnosis plot.
  • Ex-boyfriend: Caminhos do Coração and Scott Pilgrim vs. the World are high-confidence matches using literal and technological control respectively.
  • Ex-husband: the sweep found zero verified direct ex-husband-as-hypnotist titles. Desejos de Mulher remains a near-miss because the ex-husband hires a corrupt psychiatrist rather than performing the control himself.
  • Adult / erotic search: no high-confidence exact match survived the dedicated adult-audience sweep. Jacquette and The Hypnotized / Faceless Beauty remain labeled borderlines because the controller’s formal partner status is not established.
  • Other near-misses and leads: partner-commissioned control is separated from direct control; Maalaala Mo Kaya “Gayuma” uses a third-party witch doctor and love potion. Conde Vrolok and Hypnothesis remain unresolved because the required hypnosis or production facts could not be verified.
  • Coverage: seven regional and format sweeps covered roughly fifteen languages across films, shorts, television, soaps, serials, telenovelas and adult-audience material. About 91 near-misses were reviewed. Thin episode indexing in several markets remains a documentation gap, not proof of absence.
Pregnant woman hypnotized / mind-controlled: 4 stronger cases + 5 variants + 4 leads

The 30 September 2026 six-region sweep expanded the existing pregnancy-and-trance section rather than creating a parallel category. It grants pregnancy-category membership to the existing Jessica Jones, Black Magic Part 2 and Neighbours records; the 2024 Uzumaki episode is a separate record because the catalog previously contained only the 2000 film.

  • Stronger cases: The Stranger Within, Jessica Jones season 1, Black Magic Part 2 and Uzumaki episode 3.
  • Close or disputed variants: Rosemary’s Baby, American Horror Story: Delicate, the 2003 Lyn Scully hypnosis arc in Neighbours, Anything for Jackson and provisional Alem-i Cin 4. Each card states whether the gap is diagnostic hypnosis, physical restraint, reproductive coercion or unverified literal control.
  • Unresolved leads: Metamorphosis, Conde Vrolok, Mind Game and the unverified Nollywood listing She Never Knew She Was In Love With A Demon Until She Became Pregnant For Her. They are not counted as verified.
  • Adult / erotic search: a dedicated plot-index follow-up across adult-film databases, Japanese AV listings, erotic thrillers, sexploitation cinema, fetish-clip indexes and adult animation found zero net-new verified narrative title. The only exact adult-index title, Ultrasound (2021), was already cataloged in the separate adult-context pregnancy-control section.
  • Coverage boundary: approximately 90 near-misses were reviewed. Latin America, South Asia, Southeast Asia and MENA produced no verified net-new title; soap, serial and older regional-horror documentation remains thin. These are documentation gaps, not proof of absence.
Pregnant woman controlled — adult context: 11 supported titles + 2 provisional / implied leads

The 30 September 2026 worldwide indexed sweep found 13 net-new mainstream adult-context films, television episodes, serials and anime in which a woman is pregnant while controlled or the control causes or targets the pregnancy. Three are literal-hypnosis core cases; eight are supported broader mind-control, possession or supernatural-control variants; two remain provisional or implied. “Adult context” does not claim a literal MPAA R rating for every title. The cards state the available rating evidence; pornography was excluded.

  • Evidence profile: the research assigned seven high, five medium-high and one medium confidence, but Laal Ishq remains provisional and Hell Girl is only implied, so they are separated from the 11 supported titles. All 13 findings were checked against the 805-record pre-edit catalog and are new records. Kavach… Mahashivratri / Kavach 2 is distinct from the 2016 Kavach… Kaali Shaktiyon Se season; “Shaitan Ki Beti” is distinct from the two previously cataloged Laal Ishq episodes.
  • Mechanism groups: three literal-hypnosis core cases; one alien-parasite variant; one direct demonic-possession variant; five spirit, ghost, djinn or black-magic variants; one fetal-controller variant; and two separately labeled provisional or implied leads. Each record is also cross-linked into the closest existing mechanism section.
  • Key caveats: Amaunet is dormant late in Sha're's pregnancy in Stargate SG-1; the Hell Girl client's possession is implied rather than airtight; Laal Ishq remains provisional pending a detailed episode recap; and Gece Gelen: Cin Bebek falls to medium confidence under a strict literal-possession test. Sources describe Kathleen in The Devil's Doorway as 16—the adult-context label applies to the film, not the character.
  • Search boundary: 63 near-misses and 97 firm exclusions were reviewed. No net-new title survived in Latin America, Southeast Asia, sub-Saharan Africa or Australia/New Zealand; soap and serial coverage remains thin across several European, Asian, Middle Eastern and African markets. These are documentation gaps, not proof of absence.
  • Scope rule: pregnancy and control must overlap, or the control must cause or target the pregnancy. Postpartum-only control, hauntings without verified control, control of a different character, pornography and already-cataloged titles were excluded.
Mother controlled by her current husband or boyfriend: 1 low-confidence inclusion

The 30 September 2026 adult-audience sweep searched films, TV movies, series, serials, soaps and telenovelas in 15 languages. It found one low-confidence inclusion: El maleficio (1983–84). Widowed mother Beatriz marries sorcerer Enrique de Martino; the official ViX episode 21 guide says he has her “bajo su influjo” (“under his influence/spell”), but the available sources do not prove a magical override of her will, so the card does not claim a verified literal hypnosis scene.

  • Verified mechanism groups: occult / black magic by a current husband has one low-confidence inclusion. Current-husband literal hypnosis, current-boyfriend literal hypnosis, a partner hiring or directing a hypnotist, technological / sci-fi control and vampire mesmerism by a current partner each produced zero verified titles.
  • Controller is not the current partner: Hypnotic (2021), Whirlpool, The Hypnotic Eye, Stir of Echoes, The Hypnosis, Hypnotized (2004), Nightmares and Daydreams “Hypnotized”, Distorted, Siccin, Sijjin, Caótica Ana, Nights of Cabiria, Dead Again, Tales of Terror, Murderous Trance, Perfect Little Angels, The Forces of Evil; or, The Dominant Will, Orgulho e Paixão, Fallait pas! and Practical Magic all fail because the controller is someone other than the current husband or boyfriend; several also lack established motherhood or a genuine control mechanism.
  • Mother is not actually mind-controlled: The Stepford Wives (2004) reveals Joanna was never implanted; the 1975 film murders and replaces her; Hypnotic (2023) controls the husband instead; The Astronaut’s Wife threatens and telekinetically attacks Jillian without controlling her mind; and Rosemary’s Baby uses conspiracy, sedation and exploitation rather than mind control of Rosemary’s will.
  • Motherhood is not established: Amore e ipnotismo otherwise fits the husband-hypnotizes-wife pattern; King of the Zombies implies husband-caused trance; and 被催眠的她 ultimately frames the apparent hypnosis as psychosis and does not establish motherhood.
  • Reversed direction or wrong victim: Mesmerized, The Stepford Husbands, Dr. Damon’s Experiment, Mother Is Strong on Hypnotism, Hypnotizing Mother-in-Law and The Hypnotic Wife control a husband, another man or a mother-in-law instead of the partner-mother.
  • No qualifying mechanism: Sleeping with the Enemy uses ordinary coercive abuse; Lady Possessed does not make the husband the cause. The 2023 El maleficio remake keeps the same mother-and-sorcerer-husband setup but remains excluded because no source explicitly describes magical control of Beatriz’s will.
  • Scope note: “Adult-audience” is not a claim that every title has a verified literal R / 18+ certificate. Pornographic titles and explicit detail were excluded. The search covered English, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Turkish, Arabic, French, German, Italian, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai and Indonesian / Malay; empty mechanism groups are documentation results, not proof that no title exists.
Wife with children pregnant by another man: 30 verified titles + 1 lead

The 30 September 2026 worldwide multilingual sweep required all three conditions at the time of pregnancy: the woman is married, she already has at least one child, and the pregnancy’s biological father is a man other than her husband. Thirty screen titles met that test; Amor en custodia remains a separately labeled medium-confidence lead.

  • Evidence profile: the Western and Latin American sweep contributed 23 verified titles (19 high confidence, four medium-high); East Asia, Turkey, the Middle East and Africa contributed six; and South Asia contributed one high-confidence Malayalam film, Ore Kadal. Empresses in the Palace remains medium confidence because an imperial consort is not a straightforward monogamous “wife.”
  • Plot groups: the cards separate concealed or passed-off paternity, revelation and marriage fallout, pregnancies by an ex-lover, wives who leave the husband, and husband-aware or open-secret arrangements. Period and literary adaptations are labeled on their cards rather than duplicated.
  • Pregnancy-loss cases: miscarriage or stillbirth does not remove a title when the pregnancy itself is established. The relevant cards identify the outcomes for Anna Karenina, Jules et Jim and 亲爱的小孩.
  • Excluded corrections: EastEnders’ “Sheanu” arc is excluded because a 2023 retcon makes Phil, not Keanu, Albie’s father. The September 2026 Bold and the Beautiful Steffy / Carter arc is excluded because DNA ruled Carter out and paternity remains unresolved. Koi Suru Haha-tachi is excluded because the father is deliberately ambiguous.
  • Near-miss boundary: childless wives, pregnancies conceived before marriage, uncertain or husband-confirmed paternity, IVF or surrogacy mix-ups, and affair plots with no pregnancy are not counted. Strong documented near-misses include Ullozhukku, Zachariayude Garbhinikal, Mpali, Deedan and MithiJhora.
  • Coverage gaps: no verified exact match survived in Germany, Spain, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Southeast Asia, Arabic regions, Iran, Africa, anime, Hindi screen works or several South Asian regional-language sweeps. Episode-level soap documentation, Chinese vertical dramas, Brazilian SBT / Record catalogs, African soaps and Kannada sources remain thin; these are documentation gaps, not proof of absence.
Partnered woman hypnotized or controlled into infidelity: 3 accepted titles + 2 leads

The 30 September 2026 worldwide multilingual sweep found three accepted titles covering four woman-instances, plus two clearly separated leads whose screen metadata or exact relationship reading could not be fully verified. To qualify as an accepted match, the woman must have an established husband, fiancé or boyfriend, and hypnosis, mesmerism or another genuine control mechanism must cause the romantic or sexual betrayal.

  • Evidence profile: the accepted set has two high-confidence and two medium-confidence woman-instances. Intermezzo is retained as a medium-confidence lead because its indexed synopsis supplies the exact causal plot but not verified production metadata; Verliefd is a low-confidence lead because its medium, country and pronoun antecedent remain uncertain. Three titles are new catalog records; The Curse of the Jade Scorpion and Horror of Dracula gain this category without duplication.
  • Controller groups: supernatural or occult predator compulsion accounts for both Dracula films; a stage hypnotist drives the comedy case; manipulating voices drive Intermezzo; and Verliefd remains an ambiguous low-confidence lead.
  • Documented empty groups: no verified case was found for a rival lover acting as hypnotist, a husband or partner testing or entrapping the woman, an ex-lover’s revenge, or a soap or telenovela villain using hypnosis to break up a couple.
  • Near-misses: Buffy the Vampire Slayer episodes “Him” and “Something Blue” use supernatural love compulsion, but Buffy has no established partner in either episode. NBC’s Dracula (2013) gives engaged Mina a mutual, largely voluntary attraction to Grayson without a verified compelled act. Days of Our Lives has the brainwashed Princess Gina attempt to seduce John in 2019, but no completed infidelity is established.
  • Open verification: Intermezzo lacks confirmed production metadata; Verliefd lacks confirmed medium, country and pronoun antecedent; and the 1958 Dracula seduction detail currently rests on specialist fandom wikis. No qualifying Asian, Latin American, African or Middle Eastern title was verified in this pass; those absences are documentation gaps, not proof that none exist.

  • No qualifying control: Xtro, Metamorphosis and several individually checked titles including Still/Born, Bed Rest, Apartment 7A, The Omen and The Last Exorcism Part II.
Pregnant mother + child walk-in: one airtight match (Catastrophe S2E1)

The 30 September 2026 English-indexed search and a follow-up using native-language queries across 12 priority markets established one airtight exact match — Catastrophe S2E1 (2015), in which deeply pregnant Sharon is mid-coitus with husband Rob when their son walks in — alongside one strongest candidate and 24 clearly labeled partial or exclusion cases, including 10 new catalog records from the follow-up; cards are displayed in ascending release-year order within each confidence group, with undated leads last.

  • Strongest candidate: Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising (2016). Pregnancy, toddler Stella and the opening lovemaking scene are supported by multiple sources; Stella’s immediate entrance is stated explicitly in the IMDb plot summary and the associated adult-toy gag is corroborated by reviews. Because a screenplay, subtitles or direct scene check was not available, the exact timing remains unconfirmed and the title is not presented as a fully verified match.
  • Strongest new partial: СашаТаня (SashaTanya). Alyoshka’s bedroom walk-in is documented in Season 7, but Tanya’s verified twin pregnancy begins six episodes later in the Season 8 premiere; no pregnancy-period walk-in was found.
  • Native-language coverage: targeted searches covered Hindi, Turkish, Spanish, Portuguese, Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, French, German, Russian and Italian. New partials from Russia, France, Argentina, Italy, Mexico, India, Turkey, Brazil and Japan remain labeled with the exact missing element.
  • Open questions: video, subtitle or transcript access is still needed to determine whether SashaTanya Season 8, Casados con hijos S01E89, Fais pas ci, fais pas ça Season 3 or Un medico in famiglia Season 2 contains a qualifying scene. Moni Argento’s pregnancy may also be a false alarm.
  • Not promoted: A Grande Família fails because Bebel’s pregnancy is her first. Four German or Russian walk-in clips have no pregnancy, so they remain outside the catalog rather than being padded into the partial list.
Child walks in on parents’ intimate scene: 39 sourced records

The category now holds 39 records: 23 shown strict cases involving the couple’s own minor child, four dialogue-confirmed childhood recollections, six adult-offspring cases and six labeled variants or near-misses. Descriptions remain non-graphic, and every card preserves the report’s confidence level and source caveat.

  • Strict shown cases: the own-child set is split by location. Bedroom or sleeping-room entries remain the strictest group; bathroom, living-room and couch interruptions are shown separately without losing their strict own-child status.
  • Recounted events: Veronica Mars, Scrubs, Yellowjackets and Misfits confirm a childhood walk-in through dialogue or transcript, but do not show the event on screen.
  • Adult offspring: Schitt’s Creek, Seinfeld, Life in Pieces, Psych, Titus and Friends are separated because the interrupter is an adult child.
  • Other variants: Soul Food uses a kitchen; Stepmom involves a father and future stepmother; Christmas Evil leaves the exact entry point unclear; South Park S20E04 uses a consensual kink act; F Is for Family has a child already hiding under the bed; and Once Upon a Time is post-coital rather than an interruption.
  • Worldwide result: Catastrophe S2E1 is the first verified pregnant-mother strict match in the catalog and has dual membership in the pregnancy-sex section. Pabbahelgar from Iceland remains the only verified non-English strict title found in the earlier walk-in sweep; its broader native-language searches produced unresolved leads rather than additional confirmed titles.
  • Unresolved, not promoted: exact episodes remain unidentified for Oliver Beene, Ready or Not, The Oblongs, Family Matters, The Drew Carey Show and 30 Rock. The French short Surprendre ses parents en train de... has IMDb-only support. Meet the Fockers remains a prior supplied adult-son lead without enough scene detail in this report, and the alleged Blockers stinger is contradicted by available material.
  • Firm exclusions: scenes with one parent and a different partner, a child merely overhearing from outside, an unrelated child, kissing only, averted interruptions or a reversed-direction setup are not included as matches.
Pregnant sex and intimate scenes: 18 new records after deduplication

The 30 September 2026 worldwide sweep expands both existing sections to 17 entries each. Eighteen unique records are new; Outlander, Yeh Hai Mohabbatein and Badhaai Ho were expanded in place rather than duplicated. Neon Bull and Knocked Up were independently reconfirmed and needed no structural change.

  • Having sex: the character is pregnant during an on-screen encounter, or the episode’s plot and sourcing clearly establish that it happened. Subgroups separate established partners, new partners or affairs, comedy, a plot-verified non-consensual case, adult-animation / sex-work context and one timing-caveat case.
  • Intimate scenes: attempted or interrupted sex, sensual or erotic imagery short of intercourse, affectionate non-sexual romance, labor-induction discussion, and sexual fantasy remain distinct from completed sex.
  • Evidence boundaries: A Happy Event rests on one English-language review after native-language searches did not corroborate the scene; The Housemaid, Junichi and Pasión de Gavilanes rely on viewer or fan sources; 24 Weeks verifies a sex scene but not the character’s pregnancy at that exact moment. These limits are repeated on the cards.
  • Held as near-misses: Bridal Shower only implies marital relations; Kızılcık Şerbeti does not establish overlap between the romantic episode and pregnancy arc. Other rejected leads either place the scene before pregnancy, only discuss sex, use a false or performer-only pregnancy, or lack a qualifying intimate scene.
  • Coverage gaps: no source-verified African or Arabic-language case was found, and none was verified in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali, Punjabi, Pakistani, Bangladeshi or Sri Lankan productions. These are documentation gaps, not proof of absence.
  • Performer caveat: a performer being pregnant is not enough unless the character is also pregnant. Neon Bull remains separately labeled because both are true.
Category 4: mothers with children under hypnosis or mind control

The 30 September 2026 research pass found 17 higher-confidence fits and 12 separately labeled borderline or lower-confidence cases. The higher-confidence tier includes 16 English-language titles and one Spanish-language Argentine film. Every card states its mechanism and preserves source-level caveats; several obscure shorts rely only on IMDb synopsis-level evidence.

  • Strongest concentration: demonic-possession horror and witchcraft or technology-driven mind control.
  • Open leads: the Turkish/Indonesian Siccîn/Sijjin line still needs proof that the targeted wife is a mother with an on-screen child. Both versions of El maleficio need episode-level proof of direct mind control rather than deception or intimidation.
  • Research basis: indexed page content and fetched plot text; none of these findings was re-verified in a live research browser during this pass.
Category 4: regions and formats checked with no verified fit

Targeted searches found no additional verified fit in Indian regional cinema, Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Thai or Filipino film and television; Brazilian/Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Russian, Scandinavian, Middle Eastern or African cinema; or Western animation.

  • India: Shaitaan and Vash control the daughter, not the mother.
  • Korea: Hypnotized (2004) involves a married woman, but motherhood was not verified.
  • Turkey: Dabbe: Cin Çarpması involves a possessed woman not established as a mother.
  • Other checked non-fits: Ouija: Origin of Evil, The Possession, The Exorcist, Get Out, The Manchurian Candidate, Mother Is Strong on Hypnotism, Mama, WandaVision, Bring Her Back, The Babadook, Relic and Bless the Child fail the mother-as-controlled-victim rule.
Worldwide expansion: 20 strong cases + 7 borderline

The 30 September 2026 worldwide pass added 20 defensible strong cases and 7 separately labeled borderline cases. Targeted searches covered the United States and Canada, Japan, South Korea, China, India, Latin America, Turkey and the Middle East, Russia/Soviet cinema, and continental Europe. The evidence supports fewer than the requested 40–60 new titles, so the catalog is not padded with weak matches.

  • New regional coverage is still concentrated in the United States and Japan. South Korea is represented by Hypnotized (2004), and China by The Love by Hypnotic (2019).
  • The Love by Hypnotic is supported by a MyDramaList review synopsis and TV Time synopsis, not a viewed transcript.
  • Tanken Driland and Yatterman episode 55 remain trope-index-only claims and are not catalog entries until independently verified.
Husband hypnotizes or mind-controls wife: dedicated worldwide pass

This source-index pass identified six strong movie matches, two TV-movie matches and one loose, unverified serial match. Its nine findings are included in the husband-control category and keep their direct, loose or unverified labels on the cards.

  • Strong movies: Amore e ipnotismo, Sleep, My Love, both versions of The Stepford Wives, Tee Ratra and Don’t Worry Darling.
  • TV movies: The Stepford Children is a direct match under the Stepford rule; Revenge of the Stepford Wives is loose because the town’s conspiracy—not Megan’s husband—imposes the conditioning.
  • Serial: 被催眠的她 (The Hypnotized Her) is loose and unverified because no source establishes that the husband is the hypnotist.
  • All findings in this pass rest on indexed page content reviewed 30 September 2026, not live-browser confirmation. The country and original language of Amore e ipnotismo remain unverified.
Checked and excluded from “hypnotized to love”
  • Shallow Hal (2001): the man’s perception is altered; no woman is hypnotized into love. RogerEbert.com
  • Get Out (2017): hypnosis enables the Coagula procedure, not romance. Get Out Wiki
  • Office Space (1999): Peter is hypnotized into job apathy; his romance is incidental. Wikipedia
  • Shaitaan (2024): occult control is possessive but not romantic. Tupaki
Checked and excluded from “husband controls wife”
  • Dr. Damon’s Experiment (1954, The Vise, UK): re-verification shows the husband hypnotizes his wife’s lover, not his wife.
  • Hypnotic (2021, USA): the hypnotherapist is not her husband.
  • Rosemary’s Baby (1968, USA): the husband drugs his wife, but the occult act is performed by the neighbors, not him.
  • Mesmerized (1985/86), Take Her by Surprise (1967), Perfect Little Angels (1998), The Stepford Husbands (1996), Possession (2009), The Hypnosis (2023), The Hypnotic Wife, Temptation of Wife (2008–09), and Night of the Eagle (1962) also miss the requested perpetrator–victim direction or use no hypnosis of the wife.
Titles and regions still unresolved
  • The Love Letter: the 1999 film uses a letter as a love-potion metaphor; the 1998 TV movie is a time-crossed correspondence story. A different intended title would need clarification. Boston Phoenix · IMDb
  • No verified Bollywood hypnosis-into-romance title or movie matching the single-mom-remarriage pattern was found.
  • Fantasy Island S04E06 surfaced, but no accessible plot summary confirmed a hypnosis-into-love story.
  • The earlier search found no confirmed soap-opera or telenovela match for this category. That finding is now superseded: El maleficio (1983–84), its 2023–24 remake, and Desejos de Mulher (2002) are the first confirmed telenovela matches.
  • The production country and original language of Amore e ipnotismo remain unverified.

sources.description: A worldwide research snapshot spanning films, serials, television movies, series, soap operas and individual episodes across forty-seven themes. The expanded index now includes women who knowingly or unknowingly bargain with a devil- or demon-coded force to become pregnant or have a child, with the pregnancy outcome stated; women hypnotized or mind-controlled by a husband, boyfriend, ex-husband or ex-boyfriend, with direct matches separated from third-party, occult, adult-audience and unresolved variants; adult-audience films and television in which hypnosis, possession or mind control overlaps a pregnancy or causes it; the worldwide adult-audience search for mothers controlled by a current husband or boyfriend; wives who are already mothers becoming pregnant by another man; partnered women hypnotized or mind-controlled into infidelity; the 174-entry worldwide adult-audience sweep of wives and other adult female characters subjected to hypnosis, mesmerism, hypnotic suggestion, erotic supernatural thrall or explicitly framed occult trance; wives and other female characters forcibly hypnotized into obedience; stepmothers or bonus moms hypnotized, possessed, cursed or enchanted against their will; pregnant stepmothers and bonus moms; the closest documented cases of a remarried wife controlled by her new husband or a stepfather figure; a pregnant single mother controlled by her new husband or child’s stepfather; pregnant women controlled by unborn, ghost or alien children; female characters controlled by children or teens; current wives controlled or possessed by a husband’s former wife or lover; wives hypnotized or controlled by therapists; parents being intimate while children sleep; the expanded worldwide index of children interrupting or witnessing their parents’ intimate moments; adoption followed by pregnancy; human-villain hypnosis; vampire mesmerism; demonic and occult control; spirit or djinn possession; tantrik and vashikaran plots; sci-fi control; cult brainwashing; therapeutic hypnosis; fantasy enchantment; sources.research_notes_html:
Boundaries & open questions

Woman bargains with the devil or a demon for pregnancy / a child: 9 core matches + 1 failed-deal variant + 11 unresolved leads

The 30 September 2026 multilingual sweeps now support nine core records: six knowing feature-film cases, one knowing short and two unknowing fertility schemes. A high-confidence episode in which both fertility rituals fail is separated as a variant, and eleven thinner or structurally adjacent leads are not counted as verified core matches. Every card states the pregnancy outcome and the evidence caveat.

  • New verified additions: Pengabdi Setan / Satan's Slaves and Soulful are high confidence; Exorcismo Negro is medium-high confidence with a witch-mediated devil link; and the erotic-horror film Secta Sinestra / Bloody Sect is a medium-confidence tricked fertility-clinic case.
  • Failed-deal variant: American Horror Story: Coven “Boy Parts” is high confidence on plot, but Cordelia's paid and sex-magic fertility rituals do not result in pregnancy. The counterparty is practitioner Marie Laveau rather than the devil directly.
  • Source discrepancies retained: The Surrogate now says “pregnancy outcome ambiguous” because its pre-production pitch says she cannot get pregnant while release loglines say she struggles to stay pregnant. The American Horror Stories “BA'AL” card now records that Liv's husband faked the haunting; only the final beat suggests the real Ba'al may take hold.
  • Adult / R-rated / erotic search: one medium-confidence tricked case—Secta Sinestra—survived the worldwide search, but no title verified a knowing bargain. This is a documented search result, not proof that no other title exists.
  • Structural pattern: the knowing-deal protagonists are childless or barren, except the already-pregnant woman in Soulful, whose bargain seeks a healthy birth. No verified title was found in which an existing mother bargains for another child.
  • Common exclusions: the deal seeks wealth, beauty, revenge or saving a life; the child is the price rather than the object; a husband or family member makes the deal; or the woman is impregnated, possessed or cursed without making any bargain. Rosemary's Baby, Devil's Due, The First Omen, Pari, Impetigore and AHS: Delicate therefore remain outside this exact category.
  • Regional result: verified core cases remain concentrated in Indonesian / Malay-language horror, with Nigerian, Brazilian, Spanish and U.S. examples. No verified soap-opera or telenovela title surfaced, and thin regional-horror indexing remains an open documentation gap.
Pregnant sexual pleasure scenes: 5 verified additions from a worldwide sweep

The 30 September 2026 multilingual sweep added five deduplicated titles to the existing pregnancy-sex section: two high-confidence, one medium-high-confidence and two medium-confidence findings. Each card states whether pleasure is directly verified, inferred from pregnancy-era intimacy, or supported through scene dialogue and reviews.

  • Marital comedy: Catastrophe S2E1 shows deeply pregnant Sharon and Rob mid-coitus when their son walks in; it also appears in the child-walk-in category.
  • Erotic drama and arthouse intimacy: A Frozen Flower establishes the Queen’s new pregnancy before a passionate library encounter; Los días que vendrán contains explicit couple sexuality during pregnancy, though no source specifically documents moaning.
  • R-rated comedy and affair / new partner: How to Plan an Orgy in a Small Town depicts a heavily pregnant participant reaching orgasm; the Nollywood film The Pregnant Widow has a consensual steamy scene with a new partner, but its exact release year remains unverified.
  • Search boundary: 18 borderlines or unresolved leads and 81 unique near-misses were reviewed. More than 20 regional or format veins returned no verified match, including the worldwide adult / erotic plot-index pass at high confidence. This is a documentation result, not proof that no other title exists.
  • Not promoted: Titane, Jamón, jamón and Rosemary Is Pregnant Again remain outside the catalog because the pregnancy timing, pleasure element or direct participation could not be established strongly enough.
Partner hires a third party to hypnotize or mind-control wife / girlfriend: 4 verified

This worldwide multilingual sweep found four verified matches: three research additions and one upgraded existing catalog record. It is the rarest node in this trope family: stories more often make the partner the controller, use an uncommissioned villain, or rely on a communal conspiracy.

  • Verified motives: regain her love or stop her leaving (Maalaala Mo Kaya “Gayuma”); change or “cure” her behavior (While You Were Sleeping); extract a secret about a suspected rival (Tee Ratra); and malicious elimination for inheritance and another relationship (Sleep, My Love).
  • Honest-zero regions: Latin America and Spain, including telenovelas; the Middle East and Turkey; Europe; Japan; Chinese-language markets; Thailand; Indonesia; sub-Saharan Africa; and adult / erotic indexes worldwide.
  • Evidence boundary: the partner must arrange a third party and the wife, girlfriend or fiancée must herself be subjected to hypnosis, mind control, brainwashing or magical will override. Ordinary manipulation, self-performed control and the wrong target are excluded.
Female controlled by husband, boyfriend or ex-partner: direct matches, variants and honest zeroes

The 30 September 2026 worldwide multilingual sweep creates one unified partner-controller view while preserving the existing plot categories on every record. It found three newly verified relationship readings: current boyfriend Victor repeatedly hypnotizes Ciça in O Beijo do Vampiro; a psychopathic “lover” hypnotizes the woman in Silence of Sleep; and ex-boyfriend Rodrigo repeatedly hypnotizes Amália in Caminhos do Coração. Scott Pilgrim vs. the World was already cataloged and now gains explicit ex-boyfriend membership.

  • Current husband: seven direct hypnosis cases and two broader-control cases are grouped separately from one disputed synopsis and partner-instigated third-party variants. The husband re-pass found no net-new title beyond records already in the catalog.
  • Current boyfriend: O Beijo do Vampiro is high confidence; Silence of Sleep is medium confidence because the source says “lover,” not formal boyfriend. Petite Mort has been corrected to an excluded prior lead: it is a German / Austrian torture-house horror with no verified hypnosis plot.

  • Infertility-driven sequence: 19 titles involve, or likely involve, a couple who adopts after difficulty conceiving and later has a pregnancy. Where infertility is inferred rather than explicit, the card says so.
  • Same-sex and foster-to-adopt cases: The Fosters is the one same-sex-couple case; it and Parenthood include foster-to-adopt chronology.
  • Family tension: six titles connect the later pregnancy or biological child to jealousy, favoritism or conflict involving the adoptee: Ama, Ina, Anak, Malignant, Law & Order: SVU, Only Murders in the Building, Yu-Gi-Oh! GX and ThunderCats.
  • Outcome caveat: the pregnancies in Smallville and The Fosters end in miscarriage; both still satisfy the adopt-then-pregnant sequence and are labeled accordingly.
  • Open gaps: no confident example was found where adoption is used specifically to repair a marriage or stop waiting, and no core single-parent case was verified. English-indexed sources also yielded no confirmed fit in Latin American telenovelas, Turkish dizis, Korean or Chinese drama, Russian/Ukrainian melodrama, Nollywood, or continental European television.
Adopt-then-pregnant: marginal variants and exclusions

Four separately labeled cards preserve leads that approach the pattern without meeting every strict criterion: The Reaping lacks a formal adoption and involves rape; Omen IV: The Awakening uses supernatural implantation; CSI: NY lacks independent proof of adoption-before-conception; and Neighbours uses a step-parent adoption of the later-pregnant woman’s biological son.

  • Verified non-fits: Instant Family, Friends, This Is Us, The Light Between Oceans and several other common leads fail the chronology or never include the later pregnancy.
  • Surrogacy exclusions: Rules of Engagement, Shameless and Amor à Vida use surrogacy or surrogate-like arrangements rather than the requested sequence.
  • Research limit: none of the 25 displayed core and variant entries was verified in a live research browser; confidence labels reflect index sourcing, corroboration and the report’s stated caveats.
Duplicate reconciliation

Six confirmed duplicate pairs were consolidated on 30 September 2026, reducing the index from 467 to 461 records without removing any category membership, plot detail, evidence label or source.

  • Merged records: Aval / Gruham (2017), Sijjin (2023), Alone (2015), 1920 (2008), Arundhati (2009) and Kavach… Kaali Shaktiyon Se (2016).
  • Kept separate: remakes and same-title films from different years, plus records describing distinct victims, controllers or story arcs.
  • Still under review: the similarly labeled Nazar, Tantra, Qayamat Ki Raat and El maleficio records require plot-level confirmation before any further merge. Bhool Bhulaiyaa and Manichitrathazhu also retain their existing therapeutic-hypnosis and supernatural-boundary records until category placement is resolved.
Worldwide female hypnosis and mind-control expansion

The 29 September 2026 research report lists 211 findings: six in hypnotized-to-love, one in husband-controls-wife, one pregnant-woman possession case, and 203 entries across nine new mechanism categories. Two findings—The Thief of Bagdad and Don’t Worry Darling—were already in the catalog, yielding 209 net-new records. The report states that these titles were checked against Wikipedia, IMDb, episode guides and entertainment press; because it does not map individual titles to individual pages, each new card preserves that shared source basis rather than assigning a narrower citation.

  • Largest new groups: 55 spirit, ghost or djinn cases; 33 sci-fi, alien or technological cases; 29 human-villain cases; 28 Western occult cases; and 20 vampire-mesmerism cases.
  • Regional structure: the spirit-possession category keeps separate groups for Indian films, Indian television, Korean titles, Thai and Filipino titles, and Turkish, Arab, Latin and African titles.
  • Scope: verified exclusions from the report were not added. Existing catalog records and their original caveats remain in place.
India: 41 female hypnosis and mind-control titles

This 30 September 2026 source-index pass adds or re-verifies 41 unique Indian films, television series, soaps, telefilms and anthology episodes across Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Marathi and Gujarati: 37 high-confidence titles and 4 possible cases. The cards are categorized by the controlling mechanism and preserve every source-level caveat.

  • Love, marriage or relationship: five high-confidence stories place a woman under a spell or possession that drives a marriage or romantic pursuit.
  • Husband-controlled wife: Tee Ratra is now a high-confidence match: a suspicious husband commissions a psychiatrist friend to traumatize and hypnotize his wife so she reveals her secret.
  • Villain or tantrik control: nine titles use hypnosis, black magic, trance or supernatural enslavement for revenge, violence, sacrifice or another criminal aim.
  • Supernatural control: possession is the largest cluster, with film and serial entries spanning seven Indian languages. Vish and Pishachini remain possible because the available source wording does not fully establish the control mechanics.
  • Drugs or psychological manipulation: Yeh Vaada Raha is high confidence; Vish Ya Amrit: Sitara is a possible deception-based brainwashing case rather than literal supernatural control.
  • Coverage limit: English-indexed sources yielded no confirmed 1960s–70s Bollywood title. Most verified cases date from 1980–2025, and regional-language episode recaps remain unevenly indexed.
Indonesia: 8 focused female-control findings

The 30 September 2026 focused source pass contributes eight Indonesian productions across films, sinetron, web television and a YouTube short-film series. Three plots are verified by multiple sources; five remain possible because they rely on one outlet or leave the exact control mechanism unclear.

  • Love or relationship control: Ilmu Hipnotis – Gara Gara Gendam Istriku Diambil Orang and Guna-Guna Isteri Muda are possible cases involving gendam or love magic.
  • Supernatural control: Sijjin, Sewu Dino and the 2024 Guna-Guna Istri Muda are verified; Kitab Sijjin & Illiyyin remains possible on a single source.
  • Other hypnosis: Sepatu Super has a reported hypnosis-to-hatred plot, while Malam Minggu Miko confirms only an episode titled “Hipnotis Vania”; both remain possible.
  • Open gap: no confirmed Indonesian or Indian title in this focused pass showed a woman controlled by her own husband.
India: checked but excluded

The expanded pass removed leads that did not prove external control of a female character.

  • Dissociative or split-personality plots: Bhool Bhulaiyaa (2007), Manichitrathazhu (1993), Apthamitra (2004) and Chandramukhi (2005) were excluded because their resolution is psychological rather than external hypnosis or brainwashing.
  • Wrong victim or mechanism: Munjya possesses a male character; Ek Thi Daayan uses regression hypnosis on a man; Qayamat Ki Raat does not establish female mind control; and Bulbbul, Pari, Shaapit and 1920 London do not confirm the requested female-control plot.
  • Unverified: the Bengali Arundhati remake lacked a title-specific source, while L7 surfaced only through a trailer. Neither is promoted into the catalog.
Pregnant-woman control in India & Indonesia: focused regional set

The dedicated regional filter consolidates eight sourced records from two focused 30 September 2026 research passes: seven Indian titles and one Indonesian title. Six are direct, high-confidence pregnancy-and-control cases; Iblis dalam Kandungan is a medium-high-confidence attempted-possession case; and Bandh Darwaza is a conception-time close variant.

  • Indian films: Help (Hindi), Lapachhapi (Marathi) and its Hindi remake Chhorii directly overlap pregnancy with possession or supernatural compulsion. Bandh Darwaza (Hindi) is kept separate because the verified hypnosis occurs at conception.
  • Indian television: Laal Ishq, Naagin 3 and Sasural Simar Ka have episode-recap evidence for pregnancy plus possession, hypnosis, black magic or direct mental commands.
  • Indonesia: Iblis dalam Kandungan follows pregnant Amelia as a female spirit tries to enter and possess her body to claim the baby; the available synopses do not establish whether full possession succeeds.
  • Coverage limit: no additional verified Indonesian sinetron or TV movie was found, and no separate verified Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Bengali, Bhojpuri, Odia or Assamese title met the same-character, same-pregnancy test.
Indian pregnant-woman hypnosis and mind-control pass

The consolidated 30 September 2026 Indian-language pass verified six high-confidence cases—three films and three television stories—plus one Hindi-film close variant. All involve a supernatural controller: a ghost or spirit, witches, a demonic unborn child or a vampire. The same woman must be pregnant while controlled; the conception-time variant is kept separate because hypnosis is not verified after the pregnancy begins.

  • High-confidence films: Help (Hindi), Lapachhapi (Marathi) and Chhorii (Hindi). Each directly overlaps pregnancy with possession or supernatural compulsion.
  • High-confidence television cases: Laal Ishq (“Dhruv, Sonya, Unhappy Pregnant Soul”), Naagin 3 and Sasural Simar Ka. Their episode recaps establish both pregnancy and possession, hypnosis, a spell or direct mental commands.
  • Close variant: Bandh Darwaza (1990). Neola hypnotizes and impregnates Lajo; the hypnosis occurs at conception rather than during an already-established pregnancy.
  • No naturalistic case verified: the search found no Indian plot in which a husband, doctor or criminal hypnotizes a pregnant woman for abortion, baby theft or revenge.
  • Regional-language gap: beyond the Marathi film Lapachhapi, targeted searches found no separate verified Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Bengali, Marathi television, Bhojpuri, Odia or Assamese title. Hindi serials dubbed into other languages are not counted twice.
Worldwide pregnant-woman control category

With the Indian and Indonesian updates, this category contains 19 high-confidence direct-control or possession cases and 18 close or medium-confidence variants. Every card labels the mechanism and the strength or limitation of its evidence.

  • High-confidence mechanisms: demonic possession, AI brainwashing, alien or embryo influence, an unborn parasite, a demon fetus, ghost possession, black magic and direct mental commands from an unborn entity.
  • Close and medium-confidence boundary: attempted possession, conception-time hypnosis, cult or medical reproductive coercion, supernatural pregnancy with ambiguous control, haunting or influence that stops short of clear possession, and single-source cases.
  • Regional entries: Help, Lapachhapi and Chhorii are the verified Indian film cases from the latest pass, while Iblis dalam Kandungan is the medium-high-confidence Indonesian attempted-possession case.
Pregnant-woman control: checked but excluded or unresolved

These titles surfaced in targeted searches but did not prove that the same woman was pregnant while her mind or actions were controlled.

  • Focused India exclusions: Birth confirms an eight-months-pregnant woman trapped by a sinister cult but not hypnosis, commanded acts or a mind-control mechanism. Nazar, Manmohini, Kavach, Naagin 5, Divya Drishti, Tantra and other checked serials fail the pregnancy-and-control overlap. Chhorii and Lapachhapi are now included because the newer source pass explicitly supports supernatural compulsion of pregnant women.
  • Other Indian non-fits: Jadu Tona, Yehh Jadu Hai Jinn Ka!, Vish Ya Amrit: Sitara, Bhool Bhulaiyaa, Alpviram, Qayamat Ki Raat, Savdhaan India “Miseries of a Tormented Wife,” and other Laal Ishq hypnosis episodes did not establish successful mind control of a pregnant woman.
  • Indonesian screen titles: Inang, Sumala, Racun Sangga, Beranak dalam Kubur, Satu Suro, Kuyang, Hi5teria, Malam Jumat Kliwon, Dukun Beranak and the FTV Mendadak Hamil lack same-character pregnancy plus explicit mind control; Dukun is Malaysian and also splits pregnancy and possession between different women.
  • Other unverified timing: Bunshinsaba has a possessed teacher who later gives birth, but pregnancy during possession could not be established.
  • Haunted or threatened, not controlled: Magi, Cin Azabı, The Wrath, The Unborn (2003), Ma and Sakanak.
  • Fetus affected or no overlap: Delivery: The Beast Within, Gauri: The Unborn, El maleficio and El extraño retorno de Diana Salazar.
  • No qualifying control: Xtro, Metamorphosis and several individually checked titles including Still/Born, Bed Rest, Apartment 7A, The Omen and The Last Exorcism Part II.
Pregnant mother + child walk-in: one airtight match (Catastrophe S2E1)

The 30 September 2026 English-indexed search and a follow-up using native-language queries across 12 priority markets established one airtight exact match — Catastrophe S2E1 (2015), in which deeply pregnant Sharon is mid-coitus with husband Rob when their son walks in — alongside one strongest candidate and 24 clearly labeled partial or exclusion cases, including 10 new catalog records from the follow-up; cards are displayed in ascending release-year order within each confidence group, with undated leads last.

  • Strongest candidate: Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising (2016). Pregnancy, toddler Stella and the opening lovemaking scene are supported by multiple sources; Stella’s immediate entrance is stated explicitly in the IMDb plot summary and the associated adult-toy gag is corroborated by reviews. Because a screenplay, subtitles or direct scene check was not available, the exact timing remains unconfirmed and the title is not presented as a fully verified match.
  • Strongest new partial: СашаТаня (SashaTanya). Alyoshka’s bedroom walk-in is documented in Season 7, but Tanya’s verified twin pregnancy begins six episodes later in the Season 8 premiere; no pregnancy-period walk-in was found.
  • Native-language coverage: targeted searches covered Hindi, Turkish, Spanish, Portuguese, Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, French, German, Russian and Italian. New partials from Russia, France, Argentina, Italy, Mexico, India, Turkey, Brazil and Japan remain labeled with the exact missing element.
  • Open questions: video, subtitle or transcript access is still needed to determine whether SashaTanya Season 8, Casados con hijos S01E89, Fais pas ci, fais pas ça Season 3 or Un medico in famiglia Season 2 contains a qualifying scene. Moni Argento’s pregnancy may also be a false alarm.
  • Not promoted: A Grande Família fails because Bebel’s pregnancy is her first. Four German or Russian walk-in clips have no pregnancy, so they remain outside the catalog rather than being padded into the partial list.
Child walks in on parents’ intimate scene: 39 sourced records

The category now holds 39 records: 23 shown strict cases involving the couple’s own minor child, four dialogue-confirmed childhood recollections, six adult-offspring cases and six labeled variants or near-misses. Descriptions remain non-graphic, and every card preserves the report’s confidence level and source caveat.

  • Strict shown cases: the own-child set is split by location. Bedroom or sleeping-room entries remain the strictest group; bathroom, living-room and couch interruptions are shown separately without losing their strict own-child status.
  • Recounted events: Veronica Mars, Scrubs, Yellowjackets and Misfits confirm a childhood walk-in through dialogue or transcript, but do not show the event on screen.
  • Adult offspring: Schitt’s Creek, Seinfeld, Life in Pieces, Psych, Titus and Friends are separated because the interrupter is an adult child.
  • Other variants: Soul Food uses a kitchen; Stepmom involves a father and future stepmother; Christmas Evil leaves the exact entry point unclear; South Park S20E04 uses a consensual kink act; F Is for Family has a child already hiding under the bed; and Once Upon a Time is post-coital rather than an interruption.
  • Worldwide result: Catastrophe S2E1 is the first verified pregnant-mother strict match in the catalog and has dual membership in the pregnancy-sex section. Pabbahelgar from Iceland remains the only verified non-English strict title found in the earlier walk-in sweep; its broader native-language searches produced unresolved leads rather than additional confirmed titles.
  • Unresolved, not promoted: exact episodes remain unidentified for Oliver Beene, Ready or Not, The Oblongs, Family Matters, The Drew Carey Show and 30 Rock. The French short Surprendre ses parents en train de... has IMDb-only support. Meet the Fockers remains a prior supplied adult-son lead without enough scene detail in this report, and the alleged Blockers stinger is contradicted by available material.
  • Firm exclusions: scenes with one parent and a different partner, a child merely overhearing from outside, an unrelated child, kissing only, averted interruptions or a reversed-direction setup are not included as matches.
Pregnant sex and intimate scenes: 18 new records after deduplication

The 30 September 2026 worldwide sweep expands both existing sections to 17 entries each. Eighteen unique records are new; Outlander, Yeh Hai Mohabbatein and Badhaai Ho were expanded in place rather than duplicated. Neon Bull and Knocked Up were independently reconfirmed and needed no structural change.

  • Having sex: the character is pregnant during an on-screen encounter, or the episode’s plot and sourcing clearly establish that it happened. Subgroups separate established partners, new partners or affairs, comedy, a plot-verified non-consensual case, adult-animation / sex-work context and one timing-caveat case.
  • Intimate scenes: attempted or interrupted sex, sensual or erotic imagery short of intercourse, affectionate non-sexual romance, labor-induction discussion, and sexual fantasy remain distinct from completed sex.
  • Evidence boundaries: A Happy Event rests on one English-language review after native-language searches did not corroborate the scene; The Housemaid, Junichi and Pasión de Gavilanes rely on viewer or fan sources; 24 Weeks verifies a sex scene but not the character’s pregnancy at that exact moment. These limits are repeated on the cards.
  • Held as near-misses: Bridal Shower only implies marital relations; Kızılcık Şerbeti does not establish overlap between the romantic episode and pregnancy arc. Other rejected leads either place the scene before pregnancy, only discuss sex, use a false or performer-only pregnancy, or lack a qualifying intimate scene.
  • Coverage gaps: no source-verified African or Arabic-language case was found, and none was verified in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali, Punjabi, Pakistani, Bangladeshi or Sri Lankan productions. These are documentation gaps, not proof of absence.
  • Performer caveat: a performer being pregnant is not enough unless the character is also pregnant. Neon Bull remains separately labeled because both are true.
Category 4: mothers with children under hypnosis or mind control

The 30 September 2026 research pass found 17 higher-confidence fits and 12 separately labeled borderline or lower-confidence cases. The higher-confidence tier includes 16 English-language titles and one Spanish-language Argentine film. Every card states its mechanism and preserves source-level caveats; several obscure shorts rely only on IMDb synopsis-level evidence.

  • Strongest concentration: demonic-possession horror and witchcraft or technology-driven mind control.
  • Open leads: the Turkish/Indonesian Siccîn/Sijjin line still needs proof that the targeted wife is a mother with an on-screen child. Both versions of El maleficio need episode-level proof of direct mind control rather than deception or intimidation.
  • Research basis: indexed page content and fetched plot text; none of these findings was re-verified in a live research browser during this pass.
Category 4: regions and formats checked with no verified fit

Targeted searches found no additional verified fit in Indian regional cinema, Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Thai or Filipino film and television; Brazilian/Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Russian, Scandinavian, Middle Eastern or African cinema; or Western animation.

  • India: Shaitaan and Vash control the daughter, not the mother.
  • Korea: Hypnotized (2004) involves a married woman, but motherhood was not verified.
  • Turkey: Dabbe: Cin Çarpması involves a possessed woman not established as a mother.
  • Other checked non-fits: Ouija: Origin of Evil, The Possession, The Exorcist, Get Out, The Manchurian Candidate, Mother Is Strong on Hypnotism, Mama, WandaVision, Bring Her Back, The Babadook, Relic and Bless the Child fail the mother-as-controlled-victim rule.
Worldwide expansion: 20 strong cases + 7 borderline

The 30 September 2026 worldwide pass added 20 defensible strong cases and 7 separately labeled borderline cases. Targeted searches covered the United States and Canada, Japan, South Korea, China, India, Latin America, Turkey and the Middle East, Russia/Soviet cinema, and continental Europe. The evidence supports fewer than the requested 40–60 new titles, so the catalog is not padded with weak matches.

  • New regional coverage is still concentrated in the United States and Japan. South Korea is represented by Hypnotized (2004), and China by The Love by Hypnotic (2019).
  • The Love by Hypnotic is supported by a MyDramaList review synopsis and TV Time synopsis, not a viewed transcript.
  • Tanken Driland and Yatterman episode 55 remain trope-index-only claims and are not catalog entries until independently verified.
Husband hypnotizes or mind-controls wife: dedicated worldwide pass

This source-index pass identified six strong movie matches, two TV-movie matches and one loose, unverified serial match. Its nine findings are included in the husband-control category and keep their direct, loose or unverified labels on the cards.

  • Strong movies: Amore e ipnotismo, Sleep, My Love, both versions of The Stepford Wives, Tee Ratra and Don’t Worry Darling.
  • TV movies: The Stepford Children is a direct match under the Stepford rule; Revenge of the Stepford Wives is loose because the town’s conspiracy—not Megan’s husband—imposes the conditioning.
  • Serial: 被催眠的她 (The Hypnotized Her) is loose and unverified because no source establishes that the husband is the hypnotist.
  • All findings in this pass rest on indexed page content reviewed 30 September 2026, not live-browser confirmation. The country and original language of Amore e ipnotismo remain unverified.
Checked and excluded from “hypnotized to love”
  • Shallow Hal (2001): the man’s perception is altered; no woman is hypnotized into love. RogerEbert.com
  • Get Out (2017): hypnosis enables the Coagula procedure, not romance. Get Out Wiki
  • Office Space (1999): Peter is hypnotized into job apathy; his romance is incidental. Wikipedia
  • Shaitaan (2024): occult control is possessive but not romantic. Tupaki
Checked and excluded from “husband controls wife”
  • Dr. Damon’s Experiment (1954, The Vise, UK): re-verification shows the husband hypnotizes his wife’s lover, not his wife.
  • Hypnotic (2021, USA): the hypnotherapist is not her husband.
  • Rosemary’s Baby (1968, USA): the husband drugs his wife, but the occult act is performed by the neighbors, not him.
  • Mesmerized (1985/86), Take Her by Surprise (1967), Perfect Little Angels (1998), The Stepford Husbands (1996), Possession (2009), The Hypnosis (2023), The Hypnotic Wife, Temptation of Wife (2008–09), and Night of the Eagle (1962) also miss the requested perpetrator–victim direction or use no hypnosis of the wife.
Titles and regions still unresolved
  • The Love Letter: the 1999 film uses a letter as a love-potion metaphor; the 1998 TV movie is a time-crossed correspondence story. A different intended title would need clarification. Boston Phoenix · IMDb
  • No verified Bollywood hypnosis-into-romance title or movie matching the single-mom-remarriage pattern was found.
  • Fantasy Island S04E06 surfaced, but no accessible plot summary confirmed a hypnosis-into-love story.
  • The earlier search found no confirmed soap-opera or telenovela match for this category. That finding is now superseded: El maleficio (1983–84), its 2023–24 remake, and Desejos de Mulher (2002) are the first confirmed telenovela matches.
  • The production country and original language of Amore e ipnotismo remain unverified.

Parents intimate while children sleep: 6 scene-linked titles + 1 thematic near-match.

Worldwide female hypnosis and mind-control expansion — 29 Sep 2026 report: 211 findings (6 hypnotized-to-love, 1 husband-controls-wife, 1 pregnant possession, 203 across nine new mechanism categories); “The Thief of Bagdad” and “Don’t Worry Darling” already in catalog → 209 net-new; largest groups: 55 spirit/ghost/djinn, 33 sci-fi/alien/tech, 29 human-villain, 28 Western occult, 20 vampire mesmerism.

entries.summary: Widowed mother Beatriz marries sorcerer Enrique de Martino, who becomes her current husband and her children’s stepfather. ViX’s official episode 21 guide says Enrique has Beatriz “bajo su influjo” (“under his influence/spell”), but available sources do not prove that his sorcery overrides her will rather than describing domination by fear, authority or occult menace. Remarried-wife category detail: Beatriz is a widowed mother who remarries occultist Enrique de Martino, making him stepfather to Vicky and Juanito. Enrique enters the marriage partly to reach Juanito for Bael, but available sources do not establish that he directly hypnotizes or mind-controls Beatriz. New-husband/stepfather category detail: Beatriz is a widow raising Vicky and Juanito who marries sorcerer Enrique de Martino. NEAR-MISS — fails criterion 3 because Beatriz is not pregnant; daughter Vicky is the one who becomes pregnant. Criterion 5 is only partial because the plot supports occult manipulation, not explicit hypnosis or mind control of Beatriz. Mother/current-partner category detail: Widowed mother Beatriz marries Enrique de Martino and moves with Vicky and Juanito into his household. Enrique is her current husband and the children’s stepfather; he is a sorcerer devoted to Bael, and the official ViX guide for episode 21 says that he has Beatriz ‘bajo su influjo’ in Acapulco. This is a low-confidence inclusion because the phrase supports supernatural influence or spell-like control, but the available sources do not explicitly prove that Enrique magically overrides Beatriz’s mind or will rather than dominating her through fear, authority and occult menace.

entries.title: Yeh Hai Mohabbatein
entries.subtitle: Shagun possession track
entries.mechanism: Spirit / ghost / djinn possession · Ex-wife spirit possession
entries.confidence_flag: Research report · web-verified · High confidence
entries.summary: Shagun's ghost enters Ishita and controls her; she is described as "hypnotized by Shagun's ghost." Ex-wife/ex-lover category detail: After Raman Bhalla’s ex-wife Shagun dies by suicide, her spirit repeatedly possesses Raman’s current wife Ishita and takes full control of her body. Possessed Ishita calls herself “Shagun maa,” attacks Raman, flirts with Ashok and forces the vegetarian Ishita to eat chicken on Karva Chauth. Pregnant-stepmother arc: Dentist Ishita Iyer marries divorced father Raman Kumar Bhalla to secure custody of his daughter Ruhi and also mothers his son Aditya. In 2015 she becomes pregnant with Raman’s child, a celebrated pregnancy beat that ends in miscarriage after an accident caused by Ashok Khanna. During the pregnancy track, Raman hugs Ishita when the positive test is revealed, says “I love you,” imagines their baby’s future with her, and later pampers her and serves milk in bed.
entries.provenance: Wikipedia, IMDb, episode guides and entertainment press (research report, 29 Sep 2026).

entries.title: American Horror Stories
entries.subtitle: Season 1, episode 5 · “BA'AL”
entries.meta: TV anthology episode · United States · English · FX on Hulu
entries.mechanism: Unknowing fertility ritual; later knowing bargain
entries.confidence_flag: High confidence · first pregnancy YES · second outcome AMBIGUOUS
entries.summary: After five failed IVF rounds, Liv accepts a Ba'al fertility statue from a clinic receptionist and unknowingly uses it during intimacy in hope of conception. She becomes pregnant and gives birth to Aaron. In the final beat, now knowingly bound to the real Ba'al, she offers to release him if he gives her “another baby”; the episode ends before that second outcome is shown.
entries.provenance: Source sites cited in the 30 Sep 2026 worldwide sweep: thewrap.com, screenrant.com and americanhorrorstory.fandom.com/wiki/BA'AL.
entries.note: Caveat: Liv's husband faked the apparent haunting as a gaslighting scheme. Only the final beat suggests that the real Ba'al may take hold, which makes the episode a two-stage hoax / possible-supernatural case rather than an uninterrupted demonic bargain plot.

entries.note: The immediate counterparty is a witch, not Satan. The devil-link runs through Malvina's dark magic and the daughter's promised marriage to the devil's son.

sections.title: Adult female hypnosis — R-rated-equivalent worldwide
sections.description: A 174-title worldwide multilingual index: the 129-title mainstream baseline plus a 45-title adult / erotic gap-fill sweep. It covers wives and other adult women subjected to hypnosis, mesmerism, hypnotherapy abuse, hypnotic seduction, love-spell control and explicitly framed occult trance. “Adult / erotic” is a cross-country content description rather than a literal MPAA rating; mainstream non-pornographic films and adult-audience television are included.

notes.html: Research boundary: “Adult / erotic” is an adult-audience, non-pornographic scope rather than a universal certification label. Pure possession without hypnosis framing, male-only victims, fake hypnosis and teen or child victims are excluded from the gap-fill set. Africa, Pakistan, Israel and Iran produced no verified match; Spanish, Portuguese and Italian episode guides, French TV movies, Indian regional cinema and deeper anime indexes remain documentation gaps rather than confirmed absences.

sections.description: A male romantic partner pays, hires, or commissions a third party — hypnotist, psychiatrist, occultist, or other controller — to hypnotize, mind-control, brainwash, or magically override the will of his wife, girlfriend, or fiancée. Pornography was excluded. Pregnancy and control must overlap, or the control must cause or target the pregnancy.

Period and literary adaptations are labeled on their cards rather than duplicated.

sections.description: Nine core films, shorts and television episodes in which a woman knowingly or unknowingly enters a fertility bargain with a devil- or demon-coded force, plus one high-confidence failed-deal variant and eleven unresolved or structurally adjacent leads. Every card states the pregnancy outcome and its evidence caveat; the worldwide adult / R-rated / erotic sweep found one medium-confidence tricked case but no knowing-deal match.

notes.html: Adult / R-rated / erotic result: The dedicated worldwide search found one medium-confidence tricked case, Secta Sinestra / Bloody Sect, in which a Satanic-cult fertility clinic secretly impregnates the woman. No knowing-deal title survived searches of vintage erotic horror, softcore cable anthologies, adult-video plot indexes, erotic thrillers, Japanese pinku, Latin American pornochanchada and Turkish erotic cinema. Core membership requires the woman herself knowingly or unknowingly entering the fertility bargain; partner-made deals, failed rituals, a child used as payment, and forced supernatural impregnation remain labeled variants, leads or exclusions.
